methods.label: Track the total ages
methods.explanation:
Going back \(N\) years subtracts \(N\) from each child's age, so it subtracts \(3N\) from their combined age. Their current combined age is \(T\), making their earlier combined age \(T-3N\). Tom's earlier age was \(T-N\).

The statement that his age then was twice their combined age gives
\[
T-N=2(T-3N)=2T-6N.
\]
Rearranging yields \(T=5N\). Tom's age is positive, so this also gives \(N=T/5>0\), allowing division by \(N\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{T}{N}=5},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
